titleEn: A chemical fingerprint in ancient rocks suggests plate tectonics began 2.5 billion years ago
titleZh: 古老岩石的化学指纹表明：板块构造可能始于 25 亿年前
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Plate tectonics is one of the reasons Earth looks so different from its planetary neighbours.
paragraphs.zh: 板块构造是地球看起来与它的邻居如此不同的原因之一。

paragraphs.en: The movement of enormous chunks of our planet’s crust builds mountain ranges, triggers earthquakes, shapes our oceans and continents, and helps regulate Earth’s climate and magnetic field over deep time.
paragraphs.zh: 我们星球地壳的巨大块体的运动形成了山脉，引发了地震，塑造了我们的海洋和大陆，并帮助调节了地球的气候和磁场。

paragraphs.en: This process may also be key to sustaining the kind of long-term habitability that allowed complex life to evolve. But exactly when it began has been a long-standing mystery.
paragraphs.zh: 这一过程也可能是维持复杂生命进化所需的长期可居住性的关键，但它究竟是何时开始的一直是个谜。

paragraphs.en: In new research, we studied chemical fingerprints in more than 1,000 rocks to look for clues – and found clear evidence for when this remarkable shift occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 在一项新的研究中，我们研究了1,000多块岩石中的化学指纹，以寻找线索，并找到了这种显著变化发生时间的明确证据。

paragraphs.en: Why plate tectonics matters
paragraphs.zh: 为什么板块构造很重要

paragraphs.en: Many scientists believe plate tectonics provides the long-term stability that keeps our planet life-friendly, unlike tectonically “dead” worlds such as Venus and Mars.
paragraphs.zh: 许多科学家认为，板块构造提供了长期的稳定性，使我们的星球对生命友好，不像金星和火星这样的构造“死亡”世界。

paragraphs.en: But debate has raged over when this process began: has it run throughout Earth’s entire 4.5-billion-year history, or did it “switch on” at some point along the way?
paragraphs.zh: 但是关于这一过程何时开始的争论一直很激烈：它是否贯穿了地球整个45亿年的历史，或者它是否在沿着的某个时刻"开启"？

paragraphs.en: For much of its early history, Earth may have been mostly covered by oceans, without the shifting, colliding plates that build tall mountains – which in turn erode away, supplying the nutrients to feed marine life.
paragraphs.zh: 在早期历史的大部分时间里，地球可能大部分被海洋覆盖，没有移动，碰撞的板块建造高山-这反过来侵蚀，提供营养物质喂养海洋生物。

paragraphs.en: The question is hard to settle because plate tectonics are very good at destroying the evidence. Where plates collide, some old crust is dragged back down into the mantle, and the crust that is thrust upward to form mountains also starts eroding away, which erases the geological record.
paragraphs.zh: 这个问题很难解决，因为板块构造非常善于破坏证据。在板块碰撞的地方，一些古老的地壳被拖回地幔，而向上推压形成山脉的地壳也开始侵蚀，从而消除了地质记录。

paragraphs.en: Often, all that survives are chemical fingerprints preserved in ancient rocks that have endured for billions of years, against the odds.
paragraphs.zh: 通常，所有幸存下来的都是保存在古老岩石中的化学指纹，这些岩石经历了数十亿年的考验。

paragraphs.en: Reading the fingerprints in rocks
paragraphs.zh: 阅读岩石中的指纹

paragraphs.en: In our new study, we studied one such fingerprint.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的新研究中，我们研究了一个这样的指纹。

paragraphs.en: New continental crust – the ground we stand on – doesn’t always form fresh from crystallising mantle magma. Often it’s made from melting older rock that was already sitting inside existing crust.
paragraphs.zh: 新的大陆地壳--我们所站立的地面--并不总是从结晶的地幔岩浆中新鲜形成的，它通常是由已经存在于现有地壳中的老岩石熔化而成的。

paragraphs.en: That process leaves a lasting chemical trace in the new rocks, a bit like the DNA a child inherits from their parents. This is the fingerprint we studied.
paragraphs.zh: 这个过程会在新岩石中留下持久的化学痕迹，有点像孩子从父母那里继承的DNA。这就是我们研究的指纹。

paragraphs.en: In some minerals (feldspar and some sulfide minerals, in our case) this fingerprint can survive largely undisturbed for billions of years.
paragraphs.zh: 在某些矿物（长石和一些硫化物矿物，在我们的情况下），这种指纹可以在很大程度上不受干扰地存活数十亿年。

paragraphs.en: We analysed over 1,200 rocks, some newly analysed by us, others compiled from earlier studies, from ancient landmasses across Australia, Africa, North America and Europe, spanning nearly four billion years of Earth’s history.
paragraphs.zh: 我们分析了1,200多块岩石，其中一些是我们新分析的，另一些是从早期的研究中汇编的，来自澳大利亚、非洲、北美和欧洲的古老大陆，跨越了近40亿年的地球历史。

paragraphs.en: The vanishing signal
paragraphs.zh: 消失的信号

paragraphs.en: We found a striking pattern in the fingerprints. Rocks older than about 2.5 billion years carried the unmistakable signature of very ancient crust, which appears to have formed about four billion years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在指纹中发现了一个惊人的模式，年龄超过25亿年的岩石带有非常古老的地壳的明确特征，这些地壳似乎形成于大约40亿年前。

paragraphs.en: In geological terms, this is not too long after Earth itself formed. This ancient crust material was melted and remelted repeatedly, for well over a billion years, to produce the granite-like rocks that made up much of Earth’s earliest continents.
paragraphs.zh: 从地质学的角度来看，这是在地球形成后不久，这种古老的地壳物质被反复熔化和再熔化，持续了10亿多年，产生了类似花岗岩的岩石，这些岩石构成了地球最早的大陆。

paragraphs.en: Then, around 2.5 billion years ago, that fingerprint vanishes abruptly. We searched through hundreds of younger rocks without ever finding the distinctive signature of those ancient crustal reservoirs again.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，大约在25亿年前，这个指纹突然消失了，我们搜索了数百块更年轻的岩石，再也没有找到那些古老地壳储层的独特特征。

paragraphs.en: A turning point for Earth
paragraphs.zh: 地球的转折点

paragraphs.en: We think the vanishing of this fingerprint marks a fundamental reorganisation in how Earth builds continents. Before 2.5 billion years ago, our results suggest the same ancient continental material was melted over and over again, with little input from other sources.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为这个指纹的消失标志着地球如何建造大陆的根本重组。在25亿年前，我们的研究结果表明，相同的古代大陆材料一次又一次地融化，几乎没有其他来源的输入。

paragraphs.en: Then things shifted. Instead of melting ancient rocks to form new crust, the planet started producing crust from a mix of old and new sources. This is something we still see happening today at the edge of tectonic plates, where volcanoes bring fresh molten rock up from the mantle while older crust is also being recycled.
paragraphs.zh: 后来情况发生了变化。地球不再融化古老的岩石形成新的地壳，而是开始从新旧来源的混合物中产生地壳。这是我们今天在构造板块边缘仍然看到的情况，火山从地幔中带来新的熔融岩石，而旧的地壳也在循环。

paragraphs.en: As a result, the fingerprint of the ancient crust disappeared. So we believe this shift 2.5 billion years ago was when plate tectonics may have begun.
paragraphs.zh: 结果，古代地壳的指纹消失了。所以我们相信25亿年前的这种转变可能是板块构造开始的时候。

paragraphs.en: There is other evidence of major changes around the same time, too. There were more changes in rock chemistry and alterations in the thickness and composition of the crust, and Earth’s first supercontinent also formed in this era.
paragraphs.zh: 还有其他证据表明，大约在同一时期发生了重大变化。岩石化学发生了更多变化，地壳厚度和成分发生了变化，地球的第一个超大陆也在这个时代形成。

paragraphs.en: Taken together, all this evidence shows there was a turning point in how our planet works at this time. And as a result, Earth’s surface developed the environment life needed to flourish.
paragraphs.zh: 综上所述，所有这些证据都表明，在这个时期，我们的星球发生了一个转折点，因此，地球表面形成了生命繁衍所需的环境。

paragraphs.en: We still don’t know exactly what triggered the start of plate tectonics, but we’re continuing to chase an answer. For now, our results offer another piece of the puzzle of when Earth’s unique tectonic engine kicked into gear.
paragraphs.zh: 我们仍然不知道究竟是什么触发了板块构造的开始，但我们仍在继续寻找答案。目前，我们的研究结果提供了地球独特的构造引擎何时启动的另一块拼图。
